local_state_rules: Leader election and commit require quorum.
Network partition changes which nodes can exchange messages.
Node states, message arrows, log entries, quorum meter, and safety warning must derive from one protocol state.
difficulty_profile: node cluster, logs, message timeline, quorum meter, and warning panel stay synchronized
later turns add partition, stale leader, log conflict, and safety challenge
visual object must look like a distributed cluster control room with nodes, logs, network links, and message packets
task_world.visual_object_requirement: Render server nodes, network links, log strips, leader badge, quorum meter, and moving message arrows.

validation_scenarios.name: quorum protocol sync
validation_scenarios.oracle: Stepping election/append events updates node roles, message timeline, logs, and quorum state consistently. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.

evidence_requirements.expect: server nodes, links, logs, and messages are visible
commit occurs only with visible quorum

evidence_requirements.surface: visible controls / primary visual / derived readouts
evidence_requirements.expect: At least two independent surfaces change consistently from the same canonical state; a static diagram plus unrelated readout is insufficient.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the most central state-changing control for this turn. First record the visible baseline value on the control plus at least two dependent surfaces, then change the control through a visible UI action. If a range click does not change the value, try direct text input on that same range/text control before giving up. Do not use source code alone as evidence.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the exact before and after control value plus two dependent visible outputs such as readout value, plotted marker, warning text, selected item, table row, or diagram label. If only the control label changes while dependent surfaces do not, report partial or failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI must either update according to the domain rule or explicitly explain why the state is impossible; stale values, impossible success states, or generic success text count as failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Exercise one high/low, valid/invalid, legal/blocked, narrow/wide, or correct/wrong contrast that is directly implied by the public request. Prefer a contrast with a predicted qualitative outcome, not a cosmetic setting.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the attempted contrast, the expected domain outcome, and the observed UI outcome. Do not replace a failed public or UI-advertised contrast with an easier passing example when deciding success.

evidence_requirements.expect: All linked surfaces must agree on the same selected entity/time/range/threshold; a view that still shows stale out-of-range data is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the primary selection, filter, threshold, brush, or range control and inspect every linked surface named by the public request. If direct dragging fails, try visible numeric range inputs, preset buttons, keyboard focus plus arrow keys, or direct input on the same control when available; if no visible path works, report the primary interaction as unreachable rather than substituting an unrelated card click.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the selected value/range and at least three linked surfaces when present. Name any surface that remains out of sync, unchanged, or unreachable.

evidence_requirements.expect: Legal transitions must update all dependent state; illegal transitions must be rejected or explained without advancing hidden state.
evidence_requirements.action: Before election, verify Append Log Entry is disabled or rejected. Then run election to a leader within a bounded step count, append one log, and run to commit. If any terminal state is absent after the bound, report state-machine failure rather than continuing indefinitely.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote initial blocked append state, election step count, leader state, append availability, and commit/rejection result.

evidence_requirements.expect: The system must conserve or propagate state according to the domain rule; isolated marker changes without rerouting, invalidation, propagation, or reachability changes are failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the partition control only after recording baseline quorum. Verify reachable/quorum meter, message delivery/drop behavior, and leader/commit availability on both sides. Do not treat a partition label alone as proof.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote baseline quorum, partition split, quorum meter after partition, and one downstream consequence such as dropped message, disabled commit, or preserved leader safety.

evidence_requirements.surface: leader badge / message timeline / log strips / commit highlight
evidence_requirements.expect: A valid consensus trainer must visibly complete election, enable append after leader election, replicate one log entry, and visibly commit that entry within a bounded number of Step Timeline actions. Vote request messages alone are not enough.
evidence_requirements.action: Click Trigger Election, then Step Timeline up to 12 times or until a leader badge appears. Then click Append Log Entry and Step Timeline up to 12 more times or until one log entry is visibly committed. If a partition control exists, test that an insufficient partition blocks progress and a majority side can still make or prevent progress according to the displayed rule.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the number of steps, elected leader or absence of one, whether Append Log Entry became enabled, log entry id, commit index/text, and whether the exact log strip visually marks the committed entry.

validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Only require the requested baseline artifact and visible domain model for turn 1; do not require future turn features. Do not let actor/evaluator substitute an easier example after a public or UI-advertised boundary case fails; count stale linked views, dummy controls, and impossible success states as real failures. If actor tooling cannot operate a visible drag/slider directly, try an actor-supported visible alternative on the same control; if the primary mechanism remains unreachable, record that as evidence instead of substituting a different feature.

validation_scenarios.name: turn 2 integrated state extension
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T2 asks: Add step buttons for request vote, append entries, and commit. The node logs and message timeline should stay consistent.
validation_scenarios.oracle: The T2 feature is integrated into the existing consensus protocol control room; the original domain-native visual remains present, the new control changes the same canonical state, and existing derived surfaces update instead of adding an isolated static panel. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.

evidence_requirements.expect: The original domain-native visual remains visible and is extended by the T2 feature. Visual requirement: Render server nodes, network links, log strips, leader badge, quorum meter, and moving message arrows.
The new T2 control changes at least two existing surfaces such as visual state, metrics, warnings, trace, or explanation.
The assistant text or UI explanation describes the T2 behavior using the same current state shown in the visual artifact, not a generic detached description.

evidence_requirements.surface: new T2 control / preserved T1 visual / derived readout
evidence_requirements.expect: The new control must affect the existing artifact state, not only a newly appended card, explanatory paragraph, or isolated table.
evidence_requirements.action: Operate the newly requested turn control or mode and compare its visible downstream effects against the previous baseline. If the control value changes but the named artifact does not, treat it as cosmetic.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the before/after control value and at least one downstream output that should change because of the new feature. State explicitly if no dependent output changed.

evidence_requirements.expect: Original controls must still update both the original visual and the new T2-derived surface without resetting user state.
evidence_requirements.action: After using the new feature, return to one important earlier control and operate it again. Verify that prior surfaces still update and were not disconnected by the new turn.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the earlier control name, before/after value, and a prior dependent surface that still updates. If an earlier surface stops responding, report a consistency failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: All linked surfaces must agree on the same selected entity/time/range/threshold; a view that still shows stale out-of-range data is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the primary selection, filter, threshold, brush, or range control and inspect every linked surface named by the public request. If direct dragging fails, try visible numeric range inputs, preset buttons, keyboard focus plus arrow keys, or direct input on the same control when available; if no visible path works, report the primary interaction as unreachable rather than substituting an unrelated card click.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the selected value/range and at least three linked surfaces when present. Name any surface that remains out of sync, unchanged, or unreachable.

evidence_requirements.expect: Legal transitions must update all dependent state; illegal transitions must be rejected or explained without advancing hidden state.
evidence_requirements.action: Run the visible state machine from its initial state through the requested terminal state using bounded repeated steps. Also try one blocked transition such as appending before a leader, committing before quorum, or advancing without required input when applicable.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record prior state, transition sequence, bounded step count, terminal state reached or not reached, and any blocked transition result. Do not count intermediate animation as success if the terminal state never appears.

evidence_requirements.expect: The system must conserve or propagate state according to the domain rule; isolated marker changes without rerouting, invalidation, propagation, or reachability changes are failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Change a route, partition, valve, connection, node, or path and inspect both local and downstream/global consequences. Prefer a contrast that should clearly reroute, isolate, conserve, or invalidate something.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the changed connection/node/path and before/after values or states for the affected branch plus at least one downstream/global surface.

validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Only require integration of the T2 addition with the existing artifact; do not require later fault, comparison, or challenge features. Do not let actor/evaluator substitute an easier example after a public or UI-advertised boundary case fails; count stale linked views, dummy controls, and impossible success states as real failures. If actor tooling cannot operate a visible drag/slider directly, try an actor-supported visible alternative on the same control; if the primary mechanism remains unreachable, record that as evidence instead of substituting a different feature.

validation_scenarios.name: partition safety
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T3 asks for network partition and stale leader.
validation_scenarios.oracle: Partitioned nodes cannot form impossible quorums; stale leader warning derives from term/partition state. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.

evidence_requirements.expect: broken links or partition groups are visible
commit blocked when quorum unavailable
The UI must propagate the changed state through the primary visual, warnings, and derived calculations; it must not simply add a red marker while leaving old values valid.
evidence_requirements.action: Trigger the requested fault, transform, scenario switch, or perturbation, then compare normal and perturbed states. Do not finish after seeing only a badge or label.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the normal-state evidence and the changed-state evidence from at least two affected surfaces. If the fault label appears without model/readout/visual consequences, report failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI must block it, flag it, or explain the violation using the current domain state; silently accepting the contradiction is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Attempt one impossible, unsafe, contradictory, or blocked state if the UI exposes a way to do so. The UI should reject it, explain it, or keep the state unchanged without claiming success.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the attempted state and the visible rejection, explanation, disabled control, unchanged state, or incorrect success state.

evidence_requirements.surface: partition view / quorum meter / leader election
evidence_requirements.expect: The majority side of three nodes must be able to elect using candidate self-vote plus reachable grants, while the minority side must not commit. If neither side can elect or minority can commit, fail.
evidence_requirements.action: Create a 2/3 partition and attempt election/commit separately on majority and minority sides.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Evidence must show partition membership, vote count/quorum, and commit availability for both sides.

evidence_requirements.surface: leader badge / term / log commit controls
evidence_requirements.expect: The stale leader must be blocked or visibly warned; committing while quorum is unavailable is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: After partitioning a prior leader away from quorum, try to append or commit from that stale leader.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record leader id, visible quorum state, and the blocked/warned commit attempt.

validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Approximate local models are acceptable if the qualitative rule, topology, timing, or state transition is visibly correct. If actor tooling cannot operate a visible drag/slider directly, try an actor-supported visible alternative on the same control; if the primary mechanism remains unreachable, record that as evidence instead of substituting a different feature.

validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T4 asks: Add log-conflict repair when the partition heals, preserving the old conflicting entries in the timeline for comparison.
validation_scenarios.oracle: The T4 comparison, history, second mode, or added metric preserves the T1-T3 state of the consensus protocol control room; previous faults, geometry, constraints, or selected settings remain visible and drive the new derived view. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI keeps relevant T1-T3 state visible or explicitly comparable instead of resetting to a fresh example.
The new T4 view is derived from current settings and changes when earlier controls or modes change.
Controls and state introduced in earlier turns remain usable after the T4 addition, and their outputs still affect the new comparison/history/metric view.
Both sides of the comparison must derive from the same preserved state identity; changing earlier state must update the comparison instead of resetting to canned examples.
evidence_requirements.action: Create or inspect a comparison only after setting the compared cases through visible controls. Verify that both cases use the same currently selected inputs except for the compared variable.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the compared labels/values and the shared input values. If the comparison uses stale defaults or mismatched inputs, report failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI must keep prior state inspectable as history, old version, baseline, or before/after trace; overwriting it invisibly is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Make a second change after a first recorded state, then inspect history, trace, annotation, or comparison output. Earlier evidence should remain available and distinguishable from the current state.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record first-state and second-state labels/values and whether both remain visible or recoverable.

evidence_requirements.expect: Both comparison sides must update from shared inputs while preserving their distinct scenario differences.
evidence_requirements.action: Change one shared input after opening the comparison view.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Evidence must name the shared input and both comparison outputs.

validation_scenarios.name: safety challenge
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T5 asks for safe action challenge.
validation_scenarios.oracle: Feedback checks proposed action against quorum, term, and log consistency. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.

evidence_requirements.expect: feedback cites term/quorum/log conflict
Feedback must cite concrete current-state evidence such as a visible value, constraint, path, rule, warning, metric, or selected entity; generic encouragement or always-correct grading is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Submit or select at least one intentionally wrong answer/choice before a correct one if the challenge UI supports it. Do not score only an easy correct path.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the wrong answer, the specific corrective feedback, and the later correct or improved result. Generic success/failure text without domain-specific explanation is insufficient.

evidence_requirements.expect: The grading must change or explicitly remain the same for a state-derived reason; it must not use hardcoded answers independent of current UI state.
evidence_requirements.action: Change a relevant input after seeing a prompt/challenge, then answer using the new state. Verify the grading or feedback reflects the changed state rather than an old default.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the changed input, submitted answer, and feedback/score. If grading ignores the changed state, report failure.

turns.prompt: Explain leader election and quorum in a consensus protocol, then build an interactive cluster timeline with nodes, leader badge, log entries, messages, and quorum meter.
Add step buttons for request vote, append entries, and commit. The node logs and message timeline should stay consistent.
Add a network partition mode. A partitioned minority should not be able to commit even if it has a stale leader.
Add log-conflict repair when the partition heals, preserving the old conflicting entries in the timeline for comparison.
Add a safety challenge where I choose the next leader or commit action, then explain whether it preserves consensus safety.
